title: Strong Goldbach Conjecture: Every Even n > 2 is Sum of Two Primes

problemStatement.plain: Formal investigation in number theory: Strong Goldbach Conjecture: Every Even n > 2 is Sum of Two Primes.

knowledge.progressSummary: PROGRESS (open problem): symmetric reformulation (PR #33936) extended with two structural refinements — offset-parity constraint (search space halved a second time to one residue class mod 2) and prime-midpoint sufficient condition (k=0 balanced partition). All axiom-free. Conjecture itself remains open.
builtItems: symmetric_pair_offset_parity in Proofs/StrongGoldbachSymmetric.lean:224 (offset must have opposite parity to midpoint for m>2; axiom-free)
symmetricPairCount_eq_oppositeParity in Proofs/StrongGoldbachSymmetric.lean:235 (comet count = count over single residue class mod 2; second halving of search space)
hasSymmetricPrimePair_of_prime in Proofs/StrongGoldbachSymmetric.lean:264 (prime midpoint => balanced partition 2m=m+m via k=0)
symmetricPairCount_pos_of_prime in Proofs/StrongGoldbachSymmetric.lean:269 (prime midpoint has positive comet count)
insights: Strong Goldbach for even n=2m is equivalent to existence of a symmetric prime pair (m-k, m+k) with k<m — every Goldbach partition sits symmetrically about the midpoint n/2 (Goldbach comet).
The midpoint-symmetry equivalence needs no lower bound on m: for m=0 both sides are false since primes are >=2, so it quantifies cleanly over all m in N.
Strong Goldbach and its symmetric form are logically identical (strong_iff_symmetric); the reformulation halves the search space to one bounded parameter k<n/2.

For m>2 every symmetric-pair offset k has parity OPPOSITE to m: m-k and m+k differ by 2k (same parity) and are both odd, forcing m%2 != k%2. This restricts the offset scan to one residue class mod 2 — a second 2x reduction on top of k<m.
Every prime is a Goldbach midpoint: k=0 gives the balanced partition 2m=m+m, so Prime m => HasSymmetricPrimePair m unconditionally. The comet count includes k=0 exactly when m is prime.
nextSteps: Formalize a lower bound on symmetricPairCount (partial Goldbach comet asymptotic) — genuinely hard analytic NT, likely not axiom-free.
Combine offset-parity with the k<m bound to give an explicit reduced offset range (ceil((m-1)/2) candidates) and a faster decidable search.
Relate minimal offset k(m) to prime-gap bounds.
